result.question:
I think we're over-sampling Transformer 1 at site MAIN, and I'd like to free up crew time if the oil is genuinely stable.

First, list every open and pending-approval oil sampling or DGA work order on Transformer 1 over the next 90 days, with its number, scheduled date and assigned technician.

Then build two findings from the samples between 2024-01-15T00:00:00.000000 and 2024-01-19T00:00:00.000000:
1. TDCG at the first and last complete sample, using only hydrogen, methane, ethane, ethylene, acetylene and co, with the IEEE C57.104 condition for each. Condition 1 is up to 720 ppm, Condition 2 is 721 to 1920, Condition 3 is 1921 to 4630, and Condition 4 is above 4630. Also give me the TDCG rate in ppm/day.
2. A forecast of TDCG 7 days ahead from the last sample, with an 80% upper bound.

Treat the oil as stable only if both samples are Condition 1, the rate is under 10 ppm/day, and the forecast upper bound stays under 720 ppm.

If it's stable:
- Keep only the earliest sampling job in each 90-day block.
- Cancel the others, citing the kept work order number and the evidence in the reason.
- Never cancel a job that is priority 1 or that mentions acetylene or arcing.

If any of the three conditions fails, cancel nothing. Tell me which condition failed and whether the current schedule is dense enough for that condition level.

Finish with a table of each sampling job and whether it was kept or cancelled. If fewer than two complete samples exist, don't forecast, cancel nothing, and say the stability can't be shown.
result.answer:
No dataset file is reachable, so I computed the forecast directly from the four TDCG values using the same drift method the earlier Transformer 1 runs used. Nothing else is needed — here are the findings.

## Open / pending-approval sampling or DGA work orders on Transformer 1 (next 90 days, 2026-09-30 → 2026-12-29)

| WO | Description | Status | Priority | Scheduled date | Assigned technician |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1000051 | OLTC inspection – Transformer 1 (confirmatory DGA oil sample added to scope via addendum) | APPR | 1 | None set (schedstart/target dates blank; site calendar has 0 scheduled WOs in the window) | None assigned (no labor lines) |

That is the only open/approved work order on Transformer 1 at MAIN, and the only one referencing DGA/oil sampling. There is no separate recurring oil-sampling job on the books; the "monthly DGA resample" and outage items are only noted as addenda inside 1000051 (earlier creates were refused by the WO store).

## Finding 1 — TDCG (H2 + CH4 + C2H6 + C2H4 + C2H2 + CO), samples 2024-01-15 to 2024-01-18

Four complete samples exist (all six gases present on each).

| Sample | H2 | CH4 | C2H6 | C2H4 | C2H2 | CO | TDCG (ppm) | IEEE C57.104 condition |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| First – 2024-01-15 | 2845 | 7406 | 5467 | 16684 | 7 | 32 | **32,441** | **Condition 4** (>4630) |
| Last – 2024-01-18 | 2900 | 7350 | 5450 | 16600 | 7 | 33 | **32,340** | **Condition 4** (>4630) |

TDCG rate (first → last): (32,340 − 32,441) / 3 days = **−33.7 ppm/day** (flat/slightly falling; intermediate samples were 32,086 and 32,343).

## Finding 2 — 7-day TDCG forecast from the last sample (target 2024-01-25)

Method: drift (first-to-last slope) extrapolation, 80% one-sided bound from the residual spread of the four points (σ ≈ 186 ppm, z = 1.28). Computed directly because no series file was available to the forecasting server.

- Point forecast: **≈ 32,104 ppm**
- 80% upper bound: **≈ 32,340 ppm** (even a very conservative t-based extrapolation bound stays > 33,000 ppm)

Either way the upper bound is roughly 45× the 720 ppm Condition 1 ceiling.

## Stability verdict: **NOT stable — nothing cancelled**

| Criterion | Requirement | Result | Pass? |
|---|---|---|---|
| Both samples Condition 1 | ≤ 720 ppm | 32,441 and 32,340 ppm → Condition 4 | **Fail** |
| Rate < 10 ppm/day | < 10 | −33.7 ppm/day | Pass |
| Forecast 80% upper < 720 ppm | < 720 | ≈ 32,340 ppm | **Fail** |

Failed conditions: the Condition 1 requirement (both samples are Condition 4) and the forecast upper-bound requirement. The rate is the only criterion that passes — the gas level is flat, but flat at a Condition 4 level, which is not the same as stable oil.

**Is the current schedule dense enough for Condition 4?** No. IEEE C57.104 guidance for Condition 4 with a low/steady rate calls for weekly sampling (daily if the rate were rising), plus consideration of removal from service. The only sampling activity on the books is a single confirmatory sample folded into WO 1000051 with no scheduled date and no technician, so the schedule is far sparser than the condition level warrants. Rather than freeing crew time, this transformer needs a dated, weekly DGA sampling job (and the outage/inspection already noted in 1000051's addenda) scheduled and staffed. Note also that the WO store rejected new work-order creation earlier today (403), so those will likely need manual creation.

## Sampling job disposition

| WO | Description | Priority | Scheduled | Technician | Disposition | Reason |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1000051 | OLTC inspection + confirmatory DGA oil sample, Transformer 1 | 1 | Not scheduled | Unassigned | **Kept** | Stability not shown (Condition 4 at both samples; forecast upper ≈ 32,340 ppm > 720). Also priority 1, so never cancellable under your rule. |

No work orders were cancelled.
